sections.html:
Rogers is a Benton County city in the Ozarks, tied into the Northwest Arkansas metro. Its 2020 population was 69,908, which makes it the sixth largest city in the state, and the 2025 estimate of 76,956 is a gain of 10.1%. Each recent decade added people: 57.3% in the 1990s, 44.1% in the 2000s and 24.9% in the 2010s. Across Benton County the count rose from 221,339 in 2010 to 284,333 in 2020, with 332,554 estimated for 2025. The county's median household income is the highest in Arkansas.

Houses built over that many years vary a lot, and a buyer's expectations about repairs usually follow the build date. The hilly Ozark setting adds its own questions. Sloped lots, retaining walls and runoff are everyday topics here, so inspectors tend to study grading and the foundation as closely as the roof.

sections.h2: Which school district is your Rogers house in?
sections.html:
Most of the city lies in the Rogers School District. Some western parts of Rogers fall under the Bentonville School District instead, so the boundary cuts through town. Verify the district for your address before it goes in an ad or a conversation with a buyer.

People shopping in Rogers often compare it with Bentonville, Lowell and Cave Springs. They will ask about school boundaries and the size of the yearly tax bill, so keep the district name and your latest statement within reach.

Planning and building questions go to the Community Development Department at 301 W. Chestnut St. Hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. Call 479-621-1117 for the main line, or 479-621-1100 for the Risk Reduction Division, which issues building permits and inspects work.

The city requires a permit for an accessory building that is taller than 10 feet, larger than 200 square feet, fixed permanently to the ground or hooked up to utilities. Retaining walls above 4 feet and fences above 7 feet, or fences set on concrete footings, also need approval. A plain fence outside those limits does not.

Think back to what earlier owners added. A shed, a garage turned into living space or a new retaining wall may have been built without paperwork, and that can stall a sale that depends on a lender. A cash buyer can accept the house as it stands, yet it still helps to pass along what you know.

The county, not the city, sends the property tax bill. Benton County's collector works from the main branch at 215 E. Central Ave., Room 101, in Bentonville, and the phone is 479-271-1040.

Arkansas bills a year behind, so a statement that shows up after closing can still cover months you owned the house. Before the sale, ask the title company to check the current bill, and write into the contract who deals with any bill not yet issued. An open balance can come out of your proceeds at closing, which hands the buyer a clean title.

sections.h2: Reappraisal, appeals and the homestead credit
sections.html:
Every parcel in the state is revalued on a 3, 4 or 5 year schedule. Owners who think the new number is too high must have a hearing booked with the County Board of Equalization by the third Monday in August.

People who live in their home can claim a homestead credit of up to $500 off the yearly bill. Starting with 2026 tax bills the ceiling rises to up to $600. If the buyer will occupy the house, they should apply for it once they own it.

Most of the friction in a Rogers sale comes from paper, not from the building. Three phone calls answer the usual questions.

  1. Ring the Risk Reduction Division and ask whether permits exist for additions, decks, sheds and retaining walls. If work went in without one, ask what the city would want now.
  2. Ring the Benton County collector and ask whether this year's bill is paid and whether any earlier year is open.
  3. Confirm your school district, since buyers ask early.

Jot down each answer with the date and the name of the person who gave it. A buyer or title company that sees a tidy file moves faster, and a cash buyer can price the house with fewer unknowns.

Heirs have one more task. The deed or estate papers must show who has the right to sign, because closing cannot go ahead until the title is clear.

sections.h2: Selling when the house needs work or taxes are owed
sections.html:
A house with an unfinished remodel, an old roof or a back-tax balance can still sell. The questions are who takes on the work and how the money is split. A lender usually wants repairs finished before it funds a loan. A cash buyer can purchase the house first and handle the work afterward, so the price reflects the condition and you do not carry the cost.

For taxes, ask the Benton County collector for the amount owed and give that figure to the title company. The title company subtracts it from the sale price at closing, so you never have to find the cash up front. Seeing the numbers early lets you compare a cash offer with a listing after repairs and agent costs.

Recording a deed triggers Arkansas's real property transfer tax, $3.30 for each $1,000 of consideration, paid with a stamp. Decide in the sales contract who covers it.

State law does not make a seller disclose everything known about a house. The Arkansas Realtors Association Seller Property Disclosure form is widely encouraged all the same. Even in an as-is deal, mentioning leaks, foundation movement or poor drainage protects you if a dispute comes up later.

sections.h2: What an as-is cash sale looks like
sections.html:
With a cash sale there is no repair list, no staging and no waiting on a buyer's mortgage. The buyer looks at the house in its present state and makes an offer, and you choose a closing date that fits your plans. Heirs who live out of state and landlords with a tired rental are the people who use it most. Northwest Arkansas National Airport in Highfill, about 15 miles west, makes a quick trip in to handle the house realistic for owners who live elsewhere.

Collect these items before you begin:

  • The deed, or the estate papers giving you authority to sign.
  • The most recent Benton County tax statement.
  • Any permit records for outbuildings, conversions or walls.
  • A short list of known roof, foundation and drainage trouble.

On closing day, the title company pays off a mortgage and any taxes owed out of the proceeds and gives you what is left.

faqs.q: How many people live in Rogers, Arkansas?
faqs.a: The 2020 count was 69,908 and the 2025 estimate is 76,956. That ranks Rogers sixth among Arkansas cities.

faqs.q: Which county bills property tax in Rogers?
faqs.a: Benton County does. Pay the collector at 215 E. Central Ave., Room 101 in Bentonville, or use the county's online payment pages.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to build a shed in Rogers?
faqs.a: It depends on the size. A permit is needed for accessory buildings over 10 feet tall or over 200 square feet, or ones fixed to the ground or connected to utilities.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport in Highfill, about 15 miles west, handles commercial flights. Rogers Municipal Airport serves Walmart's fleet.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Rogers house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as-is to a cash buyer, though you should still share the problems you know about. Arkansas has no mandatory disclosure statute for every sale.
